public_rationale: On the ordinary task-level reading, generative AI was already being used to automate work. Klarna's May 2024 disclosure describes an existing generative copywriting tool used for most company copywriting. That contradicts the categorical sentence. It does not settle the stronger surrounding argument about replacing whole jobs or large parts of the economy.
limitations: Evidence is a customer's own deployment report, not an independent workflow audit.
The verdict depends on reading automation at the task level; whole-job autonomy is not established.

statement.excerpt: And as a reminder, generative AI is not automation.

our_interpretation: The ordinary categorical reading is that generative AI does not automate substantive tasks previously performed by people.
Automation can concern a bounded task. Human setup, supervision, or review does not automatically negate task automation.
The claim describes an ongoing technological state. I use April through June 2024, the latest completed calendar quarter before the post, rather than later capabilities.
The surrounding discussion could instead imply reliable replacement of entire jobs or economic functions; that narrower proposition is not equivalent to the categorical sentence.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes that the relevant generative AI deployments merely assist people who still execute the substantive tasks, without demonstrated task automation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented production deployment during the target period uses generative AI to execute a substantive task otherwise performed by people, without equivalent manual execution of that task.
